spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **Data Lakehouse** places an open transactional metadata layer (**Apache Iceberg**, **Delta Lake**, or **Apache Hudi**) directly over immutable Parquet/ORC files in S3/GCS.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts How Apache Iceberg Achieves ACID & 99% File Pruning on Immutable S3 (Catalog CAS -> metadata.json -> Manifest List -> Manifest File -> Parquet (128-512MB)); Bronze -> Silver -> Gold Pipeline on Shared Object Storage (Kafka / Debezium -> Bronze Iceberg -> Silver Iceberg -> Gold (Z-Ordered)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose CoW vs MoR based on your read/write ratio and CDC `MERGE` frequency. Enforce strict layer boundaries via catalog RBAC: restrict BI service accounts to **Gold** schemas, isolate backfills on Iceberg branches, and enable **Deletion Vectors** (Delta).

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore real-time lakehouse architectures, CDC ingestion, Spark shuffle skew tuning, and dimensional star schemas.

learningJourney.title: What is a Data Lakehouse & Medallion Architecture

explanation.foundation: A **Data Lakehouse** places an open transactional metadata layer (**Apache Iceberg**, **Delta Lake**, or **Apache Hudi**) directly over immutable Parquet/ORC files in S3/GCS. Object stores lack in-place updates, so Iceberg maintains an atomic `metadata.json` catalog CAS pointer -> `manifest list` -> `manifest files` (with per-file min/max column stats) -> `Parquet data files`.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Data Warehousing, Data Lake & Medallion Architecture without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, data Lake & Medallion Architecture, store data once in open table formats (Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake) on cloud object storage, using Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers to progressively refine raw events into governed, query-ready business tables.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: How to manage Compaction, Z-Ordering & Hidden Partitioning

explanation.foundation: Keep a Lakehouse fast with four automated maintenance jobs:
explanation.core:
1. **Bin-Packing Compaction**: Merge streaming 50 KB files into **128–512 MB** Parquet files (`rewrite_data_files`) to prevent planner OOMs.
2. **Z-Ordering / Clustering**: Sort rows inside Parquet by common filter keys (`customer_id`, `tenant_id`) so row-group min/max stats skip 95%+ of blocks.
3. **Snapshot Expiration & Vacuum**: Expire snapshots >7 days and remove orphan files >24h.
4. **Hidden Partitioning**: Use `PARTITIONED BY (days(event_ts))` in Iceberg so queries filtering `WHERE event_ts >= '2026-11-01'` prune partitions automatically.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Data Warehousing, Data Lake & Medallion Architecture, watch how how to manage compaction, z-ordering & hidden partitioning interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. A Data Lakehouse unifies the low-cost, open-format object storage of a Data Lake with the ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and fast SQL performance of a Data Warehouse—typically organized via Medallion (Bronze, Silver, Gold) layers.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```sql
-- Apache Iceberg table with hidden daily partitioning & maintenance procedures (Spark SQL)
CREATE TABLE silver.orders (
    order_id BIGINT,
    customer_id BIGINT,
    status STRING,
    total_cents BIGINT,
    event_ts TIMESTAMP
) USING iceberg
PARTITIONED BY (days(event_ts));

-- Periodic bin-packing compaction + Z-order clustering + snapshot expiration:
CALL system.rewrite_data_files(table => 'silver.orders', strategy => 'sort', sort_order => 'zorder(customer_id)');
CALL system.expire_snapshots(table => 'silver.orders', older_than => TIMESTAMP '2026-11-10 00:00:00');
```

learningJourney.title: Production Architecture: Medallion Governance & File Health
learningJourney.purpose: Production architecture: see how the components compose end to end under real load.
learningJourney.explanation: Enforce strict layer boundaries via catalog RBAC: restrict BI service accounts to **Gold** schemas, isolate backfills on Iceberg branches, and enable **Deletion Vectors** (Delta) or **Puffin NDV sketches** (Iceberg) to accelerate `MERGE` mutations.

ideas.title: Avoid Over-Partitioning
ideas.description: Never partition by `user_id` or `hour + country + device_type`, which creates sparse 200 KB files that destroy Parquet compression and planning speed.

ideas.title: Prevent Catalog Divergence
ideas.description: Never write directly to S3 Parquet paths bypassing the Iceberg REST / Unity Catalog—direct writes create invisible rows and stale metadata.

learningJourney.title: Problems solved & Related Concepts
learningJourney.purpose: Applied problems: connect these internals to concrete system design and debugging scenarios.
learningJourney.explanation: Explore real-time lakehouse architectures, CDC ingestion, Spark shuffle skew tuning, and dimensional star schemas.

advanced.finalSummary: Store data once in open table formats (Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake) on cloud object storage, using Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers to progressively refine raw events into governed, query-ready business tables.
advanced.summary: A Data Lakehouse unifies the low-cost, open-format object storage of a Data Lake with the ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and fast SQL performance of a Data Warehouse—typically organized via Medallion (Bronze, Silver, Gold) layers.
advanced.keyTakeaway: If latency budgets leave no room for synchronous retries, Data Lake & Medallion Architecture, store data once in open table formats (Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake) on cloud object storage, using Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers to progressively refine raw events into governed, query-ready business tables.

prerequisites.title: Distributed & Application Caching
prerequisites.summary: Caching keeps a reusable copy of data so an application can avoid repeating a database query, calculation, or network call. It can make responses faster and reduce database load. The trade-off: the copy may be out of date.
